title.back: Section check: Evidence and early connections

intro.source: 6 questions about Lessons 1–3. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 6 questions about Lessons 1–3. There is no need to rush. You can look at the lessons again and try again as often as you want.
intro.note: Intro and results follow Our World's Malay section checks word for word (content/ms/quizzes/history.json).

questions.0.question.source: You look at the photo of the Ban Chiang pot. You say, "It has painted swirls." Which word fits what you said?
questions.0.question.back: You look at the photo of the Ban Chiang pot. You say, "It has painted swirls." Which word fits what you said?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: An inference, an idea to test
questions.0.options.0.text.back: An inference, an idea to be tested

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. An inference is an idea that explains what you see. You can see the swirls, so this is an observation. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. An inference is an idea that explains what you see. You can see the swirls, so this is an observation. Look at Lesson 1 again.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: An observation, a thing you see

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The swirls are there in the photo. You can see them, so this is an observation.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. The swirls are in the photo. You can see them, so this is an observation.

questions.0.options.2.text.source: Context, where the pot was found
questions.0.options.2.text.back: Context, the place where the pot was found

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Context is where a find lay in the ground and what was near it. The photo does not show that. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Context is the place where a find lay in the ground and what was near it. The photo does not show that. Look at Lesson 1 again.

questions.1.stimulus.title.source: A made-up find from a made-up dig
questions.1.stimulus.title.back: An invented find from an invented dig
questions.1.stimulus.title.note: "Dig" is "penggalian" here (plainer than "ekskavasi" for a made-up dig); "a student" is "seorang pelajar", the course's word for learner.

questions.1.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. At the made-up site of Vessa, a team digs up a clay bowl with painted lines. It lay in a grave, next to a bronze ring. A student writes, "The owner of this bowl was a farmer."
questions.1.stimulus.body.back: This is an invented example. At the invented site of Vessa, a team digs up a clay bowl with painted lines. The bowl lay in a grave, next to a bronze ring. A learner writes, "The owner of this bowl was a farmer."

questions.1.question.source: What does the student need before they can say this?
questions.1.question.back: What does the learner need before they can say this?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: More evidence than the bowl alone
questions.1.options.0.text.back: More evidence than the bowl alone

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A bowl cannot tell us what its owner did. Other finds and records might help, and the answer may stay unsure.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. A bowl cannot tell us what its owner's job was. Other finds and records might help, and the answer might stay uncertain.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: Nothing, as the painted lines prove it
questions.1.options.1.text.back: Nothing, because the painted lines prove it

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The lines show that someone painted the bowl. They do not show what its owner did. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The lines show that someone painted the bowl. The lines do not show what its owner's job was. Look at Lesson 1 again.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: A clearer photo of the painted lines
questions.1.options.2.text.back: A clearer photo of the painted lines

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A clearer photo still shows only the bowl. It cannot show who owned it. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A clearer photo still only shows the bowl. The photo cannot show who its owner was. Look at Lesson 1 again.

questions.2.question.source: Look at the 2015 photo of the balangay planks. Which claim does it support?
questions.2.question.back: Look at the photo of the balangay planks from 2015. Which claim does it support?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: The boat sailed from Butuan to China
questions.2.options.0.text.back: The boat sailed from Butuan to China

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The photo shows planks, not a route. It cannot show where the boat went. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The photo shows planks, not a route. The photo cannot show where the boat went. Look at Lesson 2 again.

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Nobody found the pottery inside a boat. The pottery is a different find. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Nobody found the pottery inside a boat. The pottery is a different find. Look at Lesson 2 again.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: People in Butuan built plank boats
questions.2.options.2.text.back: People in Butuan built plank boats

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. You can see the wooden planks and the holes along them. They show how people built boats.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. You can see the wooden planks and the holes along them. The planks show how people built boats.

questions.3.question.source: On the lesson's map, the lines from Butuan to other places are dashed. Why?
questions.3.question.back: On the map in the lesson, the lines from Butuan to other places are dashed lines. Why?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: They show links that were possible

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The boats and the imported pottery are clues to links by sea. But no source shows one exact trip.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. The boats and the imported pottery are clues about connections by sea. But no source shows one exact journey.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: They show the exact route of one boat
questions.3.options.1.text.back: The lines show the exact route of a boat

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. No source tells us where the Butuan boats sailed. The lines show only possible links. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. No source tells us where the Butuan boats sailed. The lines only show possible connections. Look at Lesson 2 again.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: They show trips that boats made each year
questions.3.options.2.text.back: The lines show boat voyages every year
questions.3.options.2.text.note: "Trips that boats made each year" is shortened to "pelayaran perahu setiap tahun" (boat voyages every year) to keep the option short; check the meaning is clear.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The sources do not say how often anyone sailed. The lines show only possible links. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The sources do not say how often anyone sailed. The lines only show possible connections. Look at Lesson 2 again.

questions.4.question.source: The map of Melaka is dated 1604. Which time can it help you study?
questions.4.question.back: The map of Melaka is dated 1604. Which time can it help you study?

questions.4.options.0.text.source: Melaka in the 1400s, under the sultanate
questions.4.options.0.text.back: Melaka in the 1400s, under the sultanate

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The sultanate came first, in the 1400s. The map was made about 90 years after the Portuguese took the city. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The sultanate came first, in the 1400s. The map was made about 90 years after the Portuguese captured the city. Look at Lesson 3 again.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: Melaka in the time of Portuguese rule
questions.4.options.1.text.back: Melaka in the period of Portuguese rule

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The Portuguese took Melaka in 1511, and the map comes from their time. It cannot show the city of the 1400s.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. The Portuguese captured Melaka in 1511, and the map comes from their time. The map cannot show the city in the 1400s.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: Melaka today, as a heritage city
questions.4.options.2.text.back: Melaka today, as a heritage city

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The map is more than 400 years old. UNESCO's modern record tells us about Melaka today. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The map is more than 400 years old. UNESCO's modern record tells us about Melaka today. Look at Lesson 3 again.

questions.5.question.source: The 1604 map shows a big fort, a river and roads. Whose view is hard to find on it?
questions.5.question.back: The 1604 map shows a large fort, a river and roads. Whose view is hard to find on it?

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The map shows what the mapmaker chose to draw. It shows his perspective. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The map shows what the mapmaker chose to draw. The map shows his perspective. Look at Lesson 3 again.

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. UNESCO wrote about Melaka in modern times. That is a different source from the map. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. UNESCO wrote about Melaka in modern times. That is a different source from the map. Look at Lesson 3 again.

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. The map shows a fort and roads, but few homes or people at work. Their view is hard to find.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. The map shows a fort and roads, but only a few houses or people working. Their view is hard to find.

results.high.source: Well done. You can tell what an object or a map shows from what we guess about it.
results.high.back: Well done. You can tell apart what an object or a map shows from what we guess about it.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Good. You answered many questions correctly. Look at the lessons again for the questions you have not yet answered correctly, and try again if you want.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 1–3, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Look at Lessons 1–3 again, then try again. You can take as much time as you need.
